component.name: Papertrail
component.summary: Organise and read your papers, textbooks, theses and standards

description.p: Papertrail is a library manager and reader for university students and researchers. It indexes your journal articles, textbooks, theses, reports and standards where they already are, and never changes them.

ul.li: Browse, filter, tag and search a library of tens of thousands of publications
Read PDF, EPUB, DjVu, MOBI, AZW3, XPS, CBZ and FB2 files in the built-in reader
Highlight and take notes as you read, and search them later
Fill in details from Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv and Open Library, if you choose to
Split journal issues into their articles, and gather publications into collections
Copy references in Harvard, APA, IEEE or Chicago style, and export BibTeX, RIS or CSL-JSON
Move your library to another computer, even with your files in different folders
Get summaries from Claude with your own API key, if you choose to

description.p: Papertrail stays offline until you choose otherwise, and only ever sends identifiers and titles to look up details, never your files, notes or tags.

Documents read aloud, sentence by sentence, with the computer's own voices or natural voices fetched when chosen, a reading ruler, every highlight in a window of its own, a check of the library for what needs attention, court cases looked up in sources of judgments for the UK, the EU, the US and Canada, the scanned pages of partly scanned documents recognised, and an OpenAlex key of the user's own.

The words in scanned documents are recognised, in the background and as they're read, so they can be searched, selected and highlighted, and an old paper whose own text is poor can be recognised again in full. English comes with it, and 26 more languages can be fetched when chosen.

Related papers from OpenAlex, Smart Jump from a table of contents and to the heading itself, bookmarks, full screen, turning pages, forward history, sorting and filtering by rating and by when something was last read, and an issue's articles shown exactly.

Smart Jump to the figures, tables, equations and references a document mentions, its contents at Ctrl+G, two documents side by side, areas of a page kept as highlights, case law cited in the Bluebook's or OSCOLA's form, references imported from BibTeX and RIS, and new retractions pointed out.
Saved searches, a Settings window with a light or dark theme, pictures left in their colours on dark pages, and retracted publications marked on their covers.
The reader's Notes panel shows each highlight's words and its note apart, so notes are easy to read.
